visual.titulo: Where economies of scale come from

turnos.t: Where do economies of scale actually come from?

Internal economies come from the firm's own growth. Bulk buying earns discounts. Bigger machines are more efficient. Large firms borrow more cheaply, hire specialist managers, and spread advertising over more sales.

They come from the growth of the whole industry or area, so every firm there benefits: specialist suppliers nearby, a pool of trained workers, good transport links. That's why car-parts suppliers cluster around car plants.
